ownership: SMTContext and APIASTPrinter borrow the live AST manager and shared parameter/symbol services. Declaration parameter getters copy only the selected parameter storage and numerical payload, then destroy that copy. AST payloads remain borrowed from the declaration. Parameter counts read metadata without allocation; bounds checks precede selected copies. Returned symbols borrow their symbol manager.

The HWF integer conversion's static_cast<double> followed by static_cast<int64_t> can invoke undefined C++ behavior when the rounded value lies outside int64. Go uses an exact rational comparison after binary64 conversion; no defined C++ result exists for that overflow case.

ownership: The mutable interval and node bounds own their fast-float endpoints; constant interval views borrow current node bounds. The context owns its root, parameter numerals and copied polynomial coefficients, and borrows the numeric manager and resource limit.

Fast inequalities own copied scoped fast-float values through their context. Clauses borrow atom pointers, count source-style references and register each watched variable once; context close retires the owning values after nodes. Learned-clause deletion and justification lifetime remain open.

Root close precedes source-order unit then problem-clause then lemma reference release; shared inequality values close at their last reference, and remaining unreferenced context-owned values close before context numerals. Idempotent release progress preserves cleanup retries.
deviations: The config_mpff tactic variable registration now grows source-order type/watch slots and the Go root bound arrays before initialization. The config_mpff root unit/definition/queue initialization and shared clause teardown are concrete. Selected bound justification tags are ported; node search/splitting, complete explanation ownership and the full solver lifecycle remain open.

The config_mpff six named parameter updates now retain source order, defaults, partial numeric mutation and a closable refused owner. The Go context allocates its root before this pass; complete constructor allocation order, node search/splitting and full solver lifecycle remain open.

The config_mpff context now displays definitions, units and clauses through the source MPFF to_rational_string spelling, which delegates to the ordinary String formatter. Borrowed variable display and shell forwarding are concrete; search remains open.

The config_mpff context now records child creation order, displays consistent leaves with inherited bounds and exact MPFF numeral text, and omits conflicting leaves. Search, splitting and statistics remain open.

The config_mpff round-robin variable selector and midpoint splitter now use concrete FastFloat arithmetic. Integer-bound normalization, directed unbounded splits and adjacent-value refusal preserve source order; the enclosing search queue, depth/node budgets and full tactic lifecycle remain open.

The config_mpff search loop now initializes the root, selects leaves breadth-first, replays child decisions, preserves a canceled propagation queue prefix without retaining the source-local selected node, enforces depth/node limits and owns split children through cleanup. Fast and arbitrary-float checkpoints read their numeric Runtime when no shared process is bound, and read ProcessAccounting when it is bound; the pointer-free hardware context needs an explicit process binding. Standalone runtimes cannot include allocations from unrelated owners, and the complete tactic result/simplify lifecycle remains open.

A preprocessing conflict uses the existing concrete root-literal proof wrapper owned by the logical context scope, or the immediate Boolean axiom when no false-row proof exists. Nonlinear integer branching uses unconditional replay bounds to select a factor of a mismatched integer monomial, preferring the smallest bounded interval and applying the source random reservoir otherwise. New endpoint or zero-equality atoms are marked relevant and true-first without asserting either branch. The nonlinear round count is scoped and obeys arith.nl.rounds. The existing replay representation keeps speculative integer-feasibility bounds separate from the logical bounds used to choose a split.

Products with all factors fixed, any fixed zero factor, or exactly one unfixed factor are propagated during tableau replay before MakeFeasible, including when arith.nl is false. Cross-nested polynomial construction now factors repeated variables recursively using source Horner and completing-square transformations, then evaluates exact intervals while respecting existing internalized-column bounds. Direct comparison conflicts retain the active comparison premise and selected endpoint dependencies; full row/cluster traversal is recorded below. internalize_eq_eh forced difference/numeral form, eager attached-variable guard, numeral-side triangle bounds, binary bounds, true-first propagation, scoped duplicate suppression, equality/disequality events, eager restart recreation and triangle proof hints

Retained arbitrary-precision dense optimization: internalize_objective/add_objective concrete ordered terms and missing foreign-enode attachment; value, fresh edge/objective simplex tableau with manager limit, maximize and rational-only assignment projection; mk_ineq/mk_gt/mk_ge numeric/core paths and null-justification exclusion (theory_dense_diff_logic_def.h:841-1130). Model init_model(model_generator&) preserves the existing final-check/optimized assignment, registers its arithmetic factory, fixes zeros and computes epsilon in native order (823-829).

ownership: The concrete dense matrix owns its rows, edges, cell trails and scope limits. Every stored or returned infinitesimal rational copies both big.Rat components; rollback restores owned snapshots before truncating child variables and edges. The provisional model is a fresh owned value slice. No generic or callback adapter is introduced.

Dense matrix cells notify their concrete owning theory immediately at each source update, preserving occurrence/antecedent timing without a generic callback layer. The theory borrows its base/context in concrete syntax helpers and owns atom maps, occurrences, integrality flags, scopes and model numerals. Logical-context scopes own propagation and conflict justifications. Dense setup replaces only a theory with no variables or scopes before theory setup; it preserves registry order and closes the unused owner.

RDL setup closes temporary feature collectors on validation failure and success, and configures the existing owning parameter fields before assertion internalization. Dense and sparse graph routes share the checked replacement of an unused constructor-time arithmetic plugin, preserving registry order and closing the replaced owner; default, proof, ITE and simplex routes keep their existing mixed-arithmetic owner.

UFIDL setup uses the existing temporary feature collector and releases it on success or real-sort rejection. Normal and first-push integer arithmetic reuse the constructor-time concrete owner, static proofs select per-column mixed integrality before internalization, and no-UF dense input reuses the checked unused-owner replacement path. The dense early return preserves unassigned parameter fields in their existing owners.

Dense optimization shares only the concrete difference-objective compiler, copied big.Rat term/constant storage, inequality builder and owning expression-core vector with the sparse port. The compiler receives the concrete dense owner solely for native missing-variable attachment; no universal callback/generic optimizer adapter is introduced. Each dense maximize owns a fresh local simplex borrowing the manager limit, skips the null sentinel edge and saves only non-null justification ASTs. A popped bound has exactly one remaining core reference; the dense theory Close releases it and can repeat safely. Model refresh owns a new model while independently acquired old models remain unchanged.
deviations: Arithmetic copying now preserves every currently retained registered arithmetic backend: mixed/integer/real simplex, mixed/real difference graphs, dense arithmetic, UTVPI and arithmetic dummy. The copied plugins keep fresh solver data; simplex/difference/dense constructors borrow the source arithmetic parameter owner, while UTVPI keeps its constructor defaults. Source parameter updates refresh copies without destination setup overwriting them. Managed Go scalar ownership permits safe continued checks after the original solver and manager close. Non-arithmetic plugin copying and broader context-copy learned-state fidelity remain incomplete.
Integer-only difference-graph setup branches have no retained writer for constructor-only int_only=true; no unused clone specialization or universal factory/callback adapter was added.

The QF_IDL dense setup branch now selects the concrete matrix-backed theory instead of retaining integer simplex. Focused checks cover integer and real occurrence propagation, negative-cycle context conflicts, scope restoration, rational epsilon scaling through published model values, and proof/simplex/first-push route exclusions. A dense IDL SAT/model/UNSAT/pop script passes exact C++ comparison, bringing strict scripts to 101. Remaining backend-selection work belongs to the separately recorded smt_setup source units.

RDL no longer unconditionally constructs the sparse graph solver. Automatic default first-push setup uses mixed arithmetic; static setup selects the source dense, graph or mixed branch using proofs, simplex configuration, density, Boolean/arithmetic counts and ITE terms. Dense real model/scoped conflict and sparse strict rational model/scoped conflict scripts raise strict C++ runner comparisons to 103. Go arbitrary-precision concrete arithmetic represents the source small-number and multiprecision variants; the separate AS_OPTINF backend and broader setup work remain open in their owning source records.

QF_UFIDL no longer unconditionally installs the sparse integer graph. Its default/static routing and scalar settings now follow the source, including the absence of difference-counter validation and the dense branch ignoring auto_config_simplex. Exact UF-congruence/model/pop and dense model/pop C++ scripts bring the strict runner set to 105. Source new_eq_eh consumes arith.eq_bounds by creating equality-justified lower/upper bounds; Go now queues native endpoints with scoped equality premises and proof coefficients. AS_OPTINF and other setup routes remain open in their owning smt_setup source records.

This is source-fidelity callback coverage, not proof of a correct complete dense optimizer. Native quirks are explicit: objective-index assignment lookup, objective-index zero anchor, unscaled recursive numeral accumulation, no objective-constant subtraction in inequalities, has_shared=false, and rational-only assignment publication. The source explicitly leaves epsilon adjustment as TBD in maximize. The prebuilt C++ strict-real vector reports optimum5-epsilon but evaluates (< x 5) to false and emits the exact unhandled dense-mi warning from opt_solver. Go tests reproduce and record this limitation, including through configured model refresh; they do not label that strict witness valid or repair it silently. The old Go InitializeModel incorrectly recomputed its assignment, losing a non-strict optimized point; it now follows the distinct native model-generator overload. Higher optimizer orchestration, strict-model correction, LRA/AS_OPTINF backends and Go CLI optimization commands remain open in their owning source records.

Scalar equal-column advancement owns the copied-left t*sign full-expression result in a distinct tableauDelta until UpdateXTableau finishes. Its scalar work closes before child borrowing; ready permits this local through delegated primal updates, while both owning advancement entries reject preexisting locals. Scalar row iteration owns bound, coefficient and theta locals outside ready guards, with an explicit iteration entry guard; base and queue borrowers close before locals. Copied-left scalar subtraction and division retain separate returned-reference values; division borrows its scalar denominator. Live output aliases and actual older caller comparisons retain source publication and ownership. ownership: Diagonal tail owns coefficient and debug reciprocal in a borrowed manager. Exact construction copies the by-value parameter before its member and destroys the parameter after debug reciprocal construction. Matrix owns only new numerical calls/lexical temporaries; destination owns completed/partial quotient fields. Close releases stopped calls/work, reciprocal then coefficient and roots, preserving caller values. Pair division publishes X before Y. Foreign/stopped indexed destinations reject before tail arithmetic and retain their original receipts.

FloatLU borrows static source/settings, owns permutations and U, and publishes conjugated eta/dense tails in source order. Failed dense construction/factorization retains the attempted block without publishing it. Close releases floating Go storage; operations after error/Close return explicit stopped/closed errors. Exact numerical LU ownership is not claimed.

Exact LU borrows static coefficients/settings/manager. Construct Q,R,RWave before U; construct exact work vectors only after U succeeds. Partial U, unpublished eta/dense blocks and completed tail prefixes retain separate child numerical receipts. Typed scalar/pair owners transfer actual coefficient tails without numeric copies, close published tails forward, then unpublished children, work members, U and reverse-order permutations. LU captures no delegated numerical receipts; source/caller older receipts remain independently owned.

Entering-column destinations/workspace are borrowed owning indexed vectors. Extension publishes Dim before U resize, then typed Q/R resize and row work; owned extension vector resizes before replacements. Each child retains its actual pending numerical calls. deviations: Retained trace controls use native map tag state with C-string keys, lazy table initialization and source finalize/all-flag order. MPN div_n TRACE emits every source-defined insertion through the opening numerator bracket. The next C++ display_raw read requests limb m+n from a logical m+n buffer and is undefined; Go returns arena.ErrBounds at that boundary, suppressing later borrow/newline/footer output. This is the complete defined behavior of this reached call site, not a port of the invalid read.

Nested factory traces exposed independently cached stream errors.
